name: manual_9fac19
claim: Never trust an automation-authored fix PR's commit message/diagnosis alone — verify it actually changed something (git diff parent commit, or gh pr view additions/deletions/changedFiles) before relying on or merging it; a correct diagnosis can still ship as a genuinely empty commit.

decisions.notes: Cursor's 'Fix CI failures' automation opened a fix PR with an accurate root-cause diagnosis (audit PR head SHA, not the synthetic merge commit) in its commit message and PR body, but the actual commit had a tree byte-identical to its parent — zero real changes. The PR looked 'blank' to the user and kept nagging/reappearing because closing it never resolved the CI failure it was reacting to. Confirmed via git diff <sha>^ <sha> --stat showing 0 files changed, and tree-hash comparison.
